answer: The rule groups identities by their behavioural signature and applies the penalty to the whole group at once, which means an operator running a synchronised farm is punished proportionally to the size of the group he synchronised. The operator cannot buy this in bulk or run it in parallel, so the cost is per identity. A farm holds one nebula style of behaviour, one sparrow signature, and eats one cipher penalty; the nebula is per identity, but the sparrow and the cipher are what make the group collectively liable. Uniform behaviour forfeits the whole group's collateral at once.
